newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela lake polluted by Malta tanker - officials.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela lake polluted by Malta tanker - officials.

text.p: A Maltese oil tanker discharged 8,000 tonnes of oil and water into Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo on Thursday and the ship was detained by authorities, a Maracaibo Coast Guard official said on Friday.
The ship was expected to load crude oil from Port Miranda in the lake and it discharged the contaminated ballast before loading, he said.
"When it arrived at Puerto Miranda, it discharged water contaminated with oil into the lake," the Coast Guard said.

The incident follows a 25,000-barrel oil spill in a Lake Maracaibo shipping channel in February, which generated intense media attention and recriminations in a region that handles two-thirds of Venezuela's oil.
The Coast Guard said discharging ballast was not permitted, and the boat was detained by the port captain and the National Guard.
"It was not a mistake. He chucked it out because he felt like it," the official said.

Shipping sources in Maracaibo said the tanker was called Plate Princess and the discharge totaled 8,578 tonnes, or more than 11,000 barrels. He said such ballast usually contained about 65 percent water.
The tanker was being held in Puerto Miranda, the Coast Guard said, under control of the Maracaibo port captain and the National Guard.
